gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Apex 300's built-in solar input, which every Apex 300 + B300K 5.5 kWh panel kit charges through, takes only panels or strings with an open-circuit voltage of 60 V or less on two XT60 ports. In default (non-Advanced) mode the manual caps current at 8.2 A when the input is 12–30 V, rising to 20 A at 30–60 V, so low-voltage panels on a port charge slowly unless they are wired in series or Advanced mode is switched on.
standout_why: I compared against StormWatts '5 kWh-Class Solar Generators Compared on Solar Input' (cited), EnergySage 'Best Solar Generators In 2026' (cited) and BLUETTI's own Apex 300 pages. StormWatts gives voltage windows and panel layouts for the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus (High-PV 135–450 V, two Low-PV ports at 16–60 V and 10.5 A; Jackery's FAQ says no more than two 500 X panels), the Anker SOLIX S5000, the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 and the F3800 Plus. It does not cover BLUETTI. EnergySage gives the Apex 300 only as '2,400 W (more with SolarX 4K)' plus the add-on hub needed for USB and 12 V. Neither states the Apex 300's 60 V Voc ceiling, its XT60 input ports or the 8.2 A low-voltage cap in default mode. The BLUETTI US product pages show only '4,000W solar input — requires SolarX 4K'. Lights On Labs could not be opened (certificate error), so it is not compared.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. The Apex 300 + B300K kits (5,529.6 Wh) are pre-orders dispatching late January 2027, so they can only be the larger option for a shopper who can wait. The finding is the wiring warning that belongs in their row: keep each panel string at 60 V Voc or less, and turn on Advanced mode or wire in series so 12–30 V panels are not held to 8.2 A. The rival Jackery Solar Generator 5000 Plus kit is already covered by StormWatts' port windows. Of our kits, the BLUETTI 5kWh RV Kit (5,120 Wh, ships now) is a fixed RV install with 12 V/24 V DC output. The kit page says most RV owners can install it themselves. I could not open its solar-input window, so its panel fit stays unstated.

findings.label: Built-in solar input voltage window and Voc ceiling
findings.value: 12–60 V; 'Do not use solar panels with open circuit voltage higher than 60V'; panel requirement 'Voc: 12V-60V, Current: 20A Max., Power: 1,200W Max.'
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 Portable Power Station User Manual V2.1 (P/N 17.0303.0869-02A2), manuals.plus copy
findings.note: This is the 230 V international edition (EU/UK/AU AC limits). BLUETTI's US manual PDF was over the fetch size limit, so the US DC-input table was not read directly. The DC solar input is normally the same across regions, but the page should cite it as the manual's statement. Practical rule: a series string's total Voc must stay at or under 60 V.

findings.label: Solar/DC input current limit by input voltage and mode
findings.value: Non-Advanced (default): 8.2 A at 12–30 V, 20 A at 30–60 V. Advanced (set in the app): 8.2 A at 12–16 V, 20 A at 16–60 V.
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 Portable Power Station User Manual V2.1, manuals.plus copy
findings.note: Arithmetic: a port fed below 30 V in default mode tops out at 8.2 A × 30 V = 246 W at most, and less at lower voltage. The manual says the Advanced mode setting changes this. It also says 'Avoid mixing different types of solar panels.'

findings.label: Solar input connector and port count
findings.value: DC input 2 × XT60PM-M; the manual's FAQ says third-party panels need MC4 connectors on the panel side
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 Portable Power Station User Manual V2.1, manuals.plus copy
findings.note: So the station side is XT60 and the panel side is MC4, which means an MC4-to-XT60 cable is needed. BLUETTI sells a 20 A MC4-to-XT60 solar charging cable, which Dealectric already lists. The Apex 300 in-box list on bluettipower.com (AC charging cable, car charging cable, grounding screw, manual) names no solar cable.

findings.label: Expansion battery limit
findings.value: Up to 6 × B300K per Apex 300 (19,353.6 Wh maximum); 2 units take 12 B300K, 3 units take 18
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 Portable Power Station User Manual V2.1, manuals.plus copy
findings.note: Check: 2,764.8 Wh × 7 packs (Apex 300 + 6 × B300K) = 19,353.6 Wh, matching the manual. The manual covers B300K, B300 and B300S packs and does not mention B500K.

findings.label: Which stations the expansion battery fits (store listing)
findings.value: Listed as 'B300K for Apex 300/200', 2,764.8 Wh, $1,099.00 (compare-at $1,199.00), available
findings.source_title: BLUETTI US store, B300K for Apex 300/200
findings.note: Read with the storecheck search tool on the BLUETTI Shopify store.

findings.label: Solar beyond the built-in input, DC output, dispatch
findings.value: 'up to 4,000W solar input' requires a SolarX 4K; 'Hub D1 is required for DC power'; 'The Apex 300 is expected to ship in late January'; 'Each unit will be delivered separately'
findings.note: The page also says the Apex 300 can 'power both 120V and 240V devices simultaneously'. It does not say whether one unit gives 240 V without the Home Backup Kit. EnergySage (cited) already has 'AC-only out of the box, so USB and 12 V ports require an add-on hub', so the Hub D1 point is not new.

findings.label: Kit scope and vehicle-side compatibility
findings.value: In the box: RV5 Power Hub, B4810 LiFePO4 battery, Epanel, Epad, drilling template and three wiring packs. DC 'Rated Output Voltage' 12V/24V, 1,620 W DC output. 5,000 W continuous AC. 'For 12V auto-leveling systems with startup currents over 100A, we recommend pairing with a dedicated B1210 battery'. FAQ: 'most RV owners can install it with basic DIY skills — no electrician required'. Scalable 5–122 kWh.
findings.note: This is a fixed RV install, not a portable station. The page lists no panel cables and does not give the AC output voltage. It shows '2–5 Business Days Delivery (Except for pre-sale products)'. Its 'Pick Your Power' widget showed 'Out of Stock' with a $0.00 placeholder, while the store's product data (storecheck, same day) listed the + 2/4/6 × 100W kits as available at $3,999/$4,299/$4,599. The 'Kits we link' table records them as shipping now.

findings.label: Rival coverage check: panel limits already published
findings.value: High-PV 135–450 V, 15 A, 4,000 W; two Low-PV ports at 16–60 V, 10.5 A, 600 W each; Jackery FAQ 'supports no more than two 500 X panels'
findings.source_title: 5 kWh-Class Solar Generators Compared on Solar Input | StormWatts
findings.note: Recorded to show what the cited rival already covers. These are not new findings for our page.
